historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle nominal growth = guided c.4% copper-equivalent volume CAGR net of thermal-coal decline and price normalisation; historical CAGRs are cycle artefacts (FY2022 peak, FY2020 trough)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR -7.7% vs revenue 3yr -1.1% and EPS 3yr -71.7%: all three are measured from the FY2022 commodity peak and say nothing about trend growth. 5yr revenue +11.7% is measured from the FY2020 COVID trough.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are null because the series has negative endpoints: FY2020 owner FCF -$1,112m (reported -905 less SBC 207), FY2022 +$8,348m, FY2025 -$976m. Reported-FCF FY2021-24 averaged $6.4bn (post-interest, pre-lease principal, pre-NCI) on an average EBITDA of $21.7bn, i.e. c.30% conversion; the mid-cycle base below converts at c.25-30% net of the heavier copper-growth capex.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle normalisation after a shock-driven FY2026: EBITDA c.$19.7bn -> c.$16.5bn in FY2027, then c.2.5%/yr as copper volumes roughly double by 2035 while thermal coal runs off. Marketing EBIT at the midpoint of its $2.3-3.5bn through-the-cycle range with its RMI funding cost charged. The axes are (1) where copper, zinc and coal settle once the 2026 energy dislocation fades, (2) whether the brownfield copper pipeline (El Pachon, MARA/Alumbrera, KCC extension, Collahuasi, NewRange) delivers >1Mt by 2028 on c.$7-9bn/yr of capex, and (3) whether Marketing's $2.3-3.5bn range holds after the Viterra exit.
scenario_narratives.bull: Copper above $11,000/t sustained by electrification and AI-power demand, Marketing at or above the top of its range for a fourth consecutive year, projects ahead of schedule; EBITDA holds c.$19.5bn in FY2027 and compounds to c.$26.5bn by FY2035. Requires two independent things to go right (price AND delivery), which is why it is not weighted above 25%.
scenario_narratives.bear: China slowdown plus coal in structural decline: EBITDA back to c.$13.5bn in FY2027 with growth capex already committed, Marketing at the bottom of its range, DRC quotas and resource nationalism slowing the copper pathway. FCF is thin but positive; the balance sheet is not at risk.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a cyclical miner-trader on mid-cycle cash generation, not on a supply-shock year. The flows are 100%-consolidated owner FCF (SBC expensed, share count flat) after the financing cost of the readily marketable inventories that the company's net-debt definition nets out; net debt, leases, non-controlling interests and the Bunge stake are settled once each in the bridge. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon at 2% and 12x FCF, and the same 9.5% USD WACC applies to all three scenarios so cyclicality is charged in the flows rather than twice. Per-share values are computed in USD and converted to pence at the dated GBPUSD rate, parity-checked against the GLNCY ADR.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle EBITDA anchor (c.$16.5bn FY2027): every $1bn of sustained EBITDA is worth roughly $0.55-0.60/share (c.42-45p) at the model's 30% tax, 9.5% WACC and 12x cap.

Capex intensity: the base carries c.$8-8.6bn/yr through FY2027-31; if El Pachon/MARA are sanctioned in full (c.$13.5bn combined) on top of the c.$6.8bn/yr industrial run-rate, FCF in those years is lower than modelled, with the payoff arriving after the explicit horizon.

RMI carry treatment: charging c.$2.0bn/yr of inventory funding cost in the flows is worth c.$1.5-1.7/share versus the sell-side convention of netting RMI against debt for free; the house view is that a $32bn debt-funded inventory book is not costless.
Terminal cap at 12x FCF (Gordon at 9.5%/2% would give 13.6x): a re-rating to copper-pure-play multiples is a bull-case item, not a base assumption.
FX: the GBp quote moves with GBPUSD independently of the USD valuation; refresh_price.py does not update fx_rate.
Coal: c.35% of Industrial EBITDA with ESG cost-of-capital pressure; a forced separation at a discount is not modelled.
NCI estimate: book NCI is negative, so the -$5.5bn bridge item is a capitalised-profit judgment (c.$0.7bn/yr at 8x); KCC's Gecamines interest and the EVR minorities are the swing items.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, LSE regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 332.2-707.2p. FX from Yahoo GBPUSD=X at the time stated in fx_note; ADR parity from GLNCY.
data_sources.financials: GLEN.L_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis (FY2018-FY2025 annual, H1 FY2025, H1 FY2026); H1 2026 interim report for the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet (net funding/net debt/RMI reconciliation, lease liabilities, other investments note 12, EPS note 17); FY2025 annual report for SBC, buybacks, cash tax, capex; H1 2026 results presentation for the c.$6.8bn/yr 2026-28 industrial capex guidance and the FY2026 illustrative EBITDA.
data_sources.qualitative: GLEN.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): business model, December 2025 Capital Markets Day copper pathway, FY2026 production and marketing guidance, bull/bear cases.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 Jun 2026: 12,993m issued less 1,267m treasury/Trust shares = 11,726m, plus 88m dilutive equity awards (H1 2026 note 17). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so buybacks (the $500m programme to Feb 2027) are value-neutral here.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company-defined Net debt $10,194m at 30 Jun 2026 (Net funding $42,418m = borrowings $45,256m - cash $3,626m + proportionate adj $788m, LESS readily marketable inventories $32,224m; includes $1,208m marketing lease liabilities) PLUS $888m industrial lease liabilities (total leases $2,096m less the $1,208m already inside net funding). RMI is netted because its carry cost is charged inside the flows (see lease_cost_pct_path note) -- deducting the funding AND charging the carry would double-count. total_debt = borrowings $45,256m + industrial leases $888m; total_debt - cash - RMI + proportionate adj = net_debt.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF 5,642 - capex 5,932 = -290) - SBC 686 - interest income 0. FY2025 is NOT the base year: OCF carried a c.$4bn working-capital build (RMI revaluation) and FY2025 EBITDA of $13.5bn was a below-mid-cycle year. The forward build is from components anchored to a mid-cycle EBITDA of c.$16.5bn.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash-flow statement, share-based payment add-back $686m (FY2024 $564m, FY2023 $742m); no separate equity-award tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income $517m is NOT stripped: Glencore is a net-debt company (net funding $42bn) and interest income on operating cash nets inside net finance costs of $2.7bn. Only the RMI carry (see below) is charged in the flows; interest on the $11bn net debt is paid for by the net-debt deduction.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow on own-share purchases $1,992m; H1 2026 $48m; a further $500m buyback announced Aug 2026 to complete by Feb 2027. Repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.fx_note: USD per share -> GBp at 100 / GBPUSD 1.3233 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09T21:29Z) = 75.57. Parity check: LSE close in pence x 1.3233 / 100 = $7.736 vs GLNCY ADR $15.48 / 2 shares = $7.74 (0.05% tie, 2026-10-09). Secondary ASX listing (GLC CDIs) expected 14 Oct 2026 -- a further parity source once trading.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: risk-free 4.1% (UST 10y), ERP 5.0%, beta 1.3 (diversified miner + trading house) -> cost of equity c.10.6%; pre-tax cost of debt c.5.5% (4.2% after tax) on the $11bn net debt (RMI funding is charged in the flows, not in the capital structure); weights c.89/11 by market value -> 9.9% rounded down to 9.5% to reflect the marketing book's lower risk and investment-grade balance sheet. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is priced in the flows, not the rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease principal ($911m FY2025) is NOT deducted from the flows; ALL lease liabilities ($2,096m: $1,208m marketing inside net funding + $888m industrial) sit in net debt; ongoing lease-asset renewal (c.$1.1bn/yr of lease additions) is carried inside the capex % path; D&A includes right-of-use depreciation. lease_cost_pct_path is NOT a lease charge on this ticker -- see notes.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: -$5,500m for non-controlling interests (Kazzinc 30%, KCC 25% Gecamines, EVR 23% Nippon Steel/POSCO, others) = c.8x a mid-cycle attributable NCI profit share of c.$0.7bn (FY2023 $1,070m, FY2024 $1,060m, FY2025 $243m, H1 2026 $205m). Book NCI is NEGATIVE (-$4,911m at 30 Jun 2026, accumulated KCC/Katanga losses) and cannot be used. Flows are therefore 100%-consolidated and the tax path carries no NCI leakage.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical') with the adaptations file applied: USD flows vs GBp quote (fx_note), leases as debt (A), NCI in the bridge, non-operating asset in the bridge (Bunge stake), cyclical mid-cycle margins. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. WHY NOT A PEAK-YEAR EXTRAPOLATION: Adjusted EBITDA ran $15.8bn (FY2018), $11.6bn, $11.6bn, $21.3bn, $34.1bn (FY2022 peak), $17.1bn, $14.4bn, $13.5bn (FY2025) and FY2026 is guided to an illustrative c.$19.7bn on Middle-East-shock energy pricing; the eight-year average is $17.4bn including the 2022 peak and $15.0bn without it (both include c.$1bn of Viterra, sold Jul 2025). The base case lets FY2026 print the guided c.$19.7bn and then normalises to c.$16.5bn in FY2027, growing c.2.5%/yr nominal thereafter as the copper build (851kt FY2025 -> >1Mt end-2028 -> c.1.6Mt 2035) offsets the managed thermal-coal decline. REVENUE IS A SCALING VARIABLE ONLY: c.$250-350bn of revenue is mostly Marketing pass-through, so the margin paths are set to deliver the EBITDA path above and should be read as EBITDA targets, not operating-leverage claims. RMI CARRY: lease_cost_pct_path on this ticker carries the financing cost of the c.$30bn of readily marketable inventories that is netted out of net debt (c.73% of FY2025 net finance costs of $2,729m = c.$2.0bn/yr = 0.65-0.75% of revenue). Marketing adjusted EBIT guidance ($2.3-3.5bn through the cycle) is pre-funding-cost; netting RMI against debt without charging its carry would treat $32bn of debt-funded inventory as free. CASH TAX: 30% of EBIT (FY2022-25 cumulative cash tax c.$15bn on c.$46bn pre-tax = 32%; mining-jurisdiction rates plus Pillar Two, offset by the Swiss marketing book). TERMINAL: Gordon at 2.0% vs a 12x FCF cap (cyclical). WORKING CAPITAL: 0% capture -- RMI swings are price-driven and mean-zero through the cycle.

bear.narrative: FY2026 EBITDA c.$18.7bn as H2 energy prices normalise faster than guided, then FY2027 falls to c.$13.5bn (FY2024-25 level): a China/global demand slowdown takes copper back toward $8,500/t, thermal coal reverts to its structural decline with no security-of-supply premium, and Marketing drops to the bottom of its range once the dislocation fades. Growth capex is already committed (El Pachon/MARA under RIGI, EVR), so capex runs at 3.0-3.1% of a smaller revenue base; DRC cobalt quotas and resource-nationalism in Argentina/South Africa/Kazakhstan slow the copper pathway so EBITDA only reaches c.$14.9bn by FY2035. No solvency question: net debt/EBITDA stays near 1x even here.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue c.$309bn x 6.4% = EBITDA c.$19.8bn (guided illustrative c.$19.7bn; H1 actual $10.1bn). FY2027 normalises to c.$285bn x 5.8% = c.$16.5bn mid-cycle (Industrial c.$13.5bn at long-run copper/zinc/coal prices + Marketing EBIT c.$2.9bn at the midpoint of the $2.3-3.5bn range, plus Marketing D&A). Thereafter +2.5%/yr with margin drifting to 6.0% as copper volume growth (>1Mt by 2028, c.1.6Mt by 2035) outweighs the thermal-coal run-off: FY2035 EBITDA c.$20.7bn nominal. Capex steps from c.$7.7bn (FY2026) to a c.$8.6bn peak in FY2029 (guided c.$6.8bn/yr industrial ex-copper-growth 2026-28 + c.$1.1bn/yr lease additions + c.$1bn/yr El Pachon/MARA/Alumbrera growth spend), easing to c.2.4% of revenue (c.$8.3bn, roughly D&A) by the terminal year. RMI carry 0.65-0.70% (c.$2.0bn/yr), SBC 0.27%, cash tax 30%, WC 0%.

bull.narrative: FY2026 EBITDA c.$20.9bn, then FY2027 holds c.$19.5bn rather than normalising: copper stays above $11,000/t on electrification and AI-power demand, the Middle-East energy dislocation persists into 2027 and Marketing prints at or above the top of its $2.3-3.5bn range for a fourth year. Copper delivery runs ahead of the CMD pathway (Alumbrera already pulled into H2 2027), so EBITDA compounds to c.$26.5bn by FY2035 on the same capex % path (higher $ capex on the larger revenue base).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: the FY2026 print is substantially a one-off supply shock (Middle East), coal is c.35% of Industrial EBITDA and in managed decline, and the historical EBITDA series has spent as many years at $11-14bn as above $17bn. Bull cut to 25%: it needs sustained above-trend copper AND on-time delivery of a c.$13.5bn Argentine project set, two independent conditions. No going-concern or covenant element -- net debt/EBITDA 0.56x at H1 2026 -- so bear is not pushed higher.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
